discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 150954
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
554 AM EDT Thu Oct 15 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Scattered rain possible today, mainly west of I-69.

- There is a Marginal Risk of severe storms (mainly wind) along
  and south of US Route 24 this evening. Confidence in severe 
  weather is low.

- Turning much cooler and windy for Friday with some lake effect
  rain showers expected. Watching for frost chances, which
  appear the most possible Sunday morning, but Saturday
  morning's chances cannot be ruled out.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 245 AM EDT Thu Oct 15 2026

Surface high pressure slides eastward this morning across the 
northern Great Lakes. This allowed drier air to seep into the area 
behind the slowly southward-moving cold front from Wednesday. This 
front quickly turns around into a northward-moving warm front today 
as a deep upper low forces a surface low northward along the western 
extension of the baroclinic zone down to the Southern Plains. So, 
the attention turns to the timing of the surface warm sector's 
arrival to see if we can get surface-based or only elevated 
convection. The GFS still has areas of large scale ascent moving 
through the area this afternoon whereas the ECMWF appears to have 
most of the better lift moving north of the area. The drier the low 
levels can get and maybe lesser cloud cover before sunrise would be 
better for instability formation. Indications in both the NAM and 
the HRRR are that the surface warm front waits until 2 to 4z to get 
into our southern 1 to 2 rows of zones, which would allow a short 
time period (1 to 3 hours?) for surface-based convection after that. 
The main ingredient of concern is the shear, which the HRRR 
indicates has around 45 kts of EBWD shear. Now, because the low 
levels up to 850 mb are essentially saturated, LCLs are sub-1000m, 
but instability is 500 J/kg or below. So, perhaps there could be 
some shallow supercells or cells with embedded rotation. With the 
moist PWATs around 1.8 inches, heavy rain rates could occur, but 
cell motions are rather fast likely limiting overall flood threat; 
that and the fact that we've been dry for so long. The other 
possibility would be a moisture loaded core- collapsing damaging 
wind threat, but that weak of instability may also limit that 
threat. The cold front slides through overnight meaning the rain 
threat is out of the area by 12z Friday.

The aforementioned upper low is squeezed northeastward out ahead of 
a diving upper low from Canada. On it's back side is a strong 1040 
mb surface high indicative of relatively cold air that its bringing 
with it. This brings in a couple of hazards that we'll get to 
describing here including lake effect rain, gusty winds, and 
potentially a frost chance. For the lake effect rain, the lake needs 
to get some instability going first as well as low level convergence 
and a return of low level moisture behind the cold front. Northwest 
wind convergence combines with these features around 12z Friday and 
would expect the intensity of lake enhancement to increase through 
around 18z when the vigorous vort max swings through. Given lake 
temps of 62 degrees, BUFKIT NAM soundings indicate 15 to 25 degree 
delta T values with tall lake induced inversions during the 
afternoon. However, there are indications that dry air begins to 
work into the low levels during the evening hours after the low 
level trough moves through and trajectories go more northerly. Low 
level moisture moves out of the area and there are indications that 
rain subsides by 12z Saturday, but could see lake effect clouds 
lingering Saturday morning, especially in the west. Then, northwest 
winds swinging through Friday evening gust between 30 and 40 mph, 
highest along the surface trough, which could bring down a stray 45 
mph gust. Now, the cold air coming in Friday night has 850 mb temps 
down to -2C 12z Saturday morning before warming ensues. The pressure 
gradient slackens overnight into early Saturday morning and cloud 
cover also dissipates overnight bringing some questions about how 
scattered out clouds can be east of US-31. Given forecast lows 
securely in the 30s Friday night, we'll have to watch for frost 
chances then, but wind and cloud cover complicate chances. A dry day 
continues on Saturday and surface high pressure overhead continues 
to keep the area calm wind-wise. Which allows a second opportunity 
for frost Saturday night as the core of the cold air lifts 
northeastward. Forecast lows dip down into the 30s again, but an 
increased gradient attempts to enter from the north. This appears to 
be the only complication for another frost attempt Saturday night. 

Looking ahead, even over the next 2 to 3 days, anomalous high 
pressure building near Greenland causing blocking to build peaks 
during the 16th to 21st of October. This is about the time that the 
NAO/AO dips negative. Meanwhile, the aforementioned baroclinic zone 
has pushed eastward potentially stalling along the eastern seaboard 
and forming an upper low or continuing to push eastward. Either way, 
this allows a sprawling area of high pressure to remain across the 
area until at least around Thursday of next week and potentially 
even longer keeping dry air overhead.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 549 AM EDT Thu Oct 15 2026

No significant changes to TAFs with MVFR cigs persisting at
KSBN, but improvement occurred at KFWA. Cigs will likely bounce
around prior to the arrival of any showers and closer proximity
to the approaching front and sfc low. In the wake of the cold
front, winds will shift to more of a west or northwest 
direction and pick up with gusts of 25 to 30 kts starting to 
materialize towards the end of the period and especially beyond.


&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Gale Warning from 11 AM Friday to 2 AM EDT Saturday for LMZ043-
     046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller

spc.summary: Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and perhaps a tornado or two are possible today across parts of the mid Mississippi and Ohio Valleys. Additional storms with isolated severe wind gusts will be possible in parts of the southern Plains.
spc.text:
SPC AC 150532

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1232 AM CDT Thu Oct 15 2026

   Valid 151200Z - 161200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE MID
   MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO THE OHIO VALLEY...AND OVER PARTS OF THE
   SOUTHERN PLAINS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and perhaps a tornado
   or two are possible today across parts of the mid Mississippi and
   Ohio Valleys. Additional storms with isolated severe wind gusts will
   be possible in parts of the southern Plains.

   ...Mid Mississippi and Ohio Valleys...
   At mid-levels, a ridge will move eastward today into the Northeast,
   as a large-scale trough moves into the Great Plains. Ahead of the
   trough, a surface low will track northeastward from the mid
   Mississippi Valley into the southwestern Great Lakes. Ahead of the
   surface low, a warm front will move northward through the Ohio
   Valley. To the south of the warm front, surface dewpoints will be in
   the upper 60s and lower 70s F. This will enable an axis of
   instability to develop by afternoon, with MLCAPE likely peaking
   around 1000 J/kg. Ahead of the trough, a mid-level jet will
   overspread the warm sector during the afternoon. This will create
   moderate deep-layer shear over much of the Ohio Valley, which will
   support isolated supercell development. In addition, RAP forecast
   soundings in the Ohio Valley by mid afternoon have 0-3 km
   storm-relative helicity in the 200 to 250 m2/s2 range suggesting
   that a tornado or two will be possible. Short line segments capable
   of isolated severe wind gusts will also be possible. Poor lapse
   rates will be the main limiting factor for a greater severe threat
   coverage and magnitude.

   ...Southern Plains...
   An upper-level trough will move into the Great Plains today, as
   mid-level flow remains southwesterly ahead of the trough. At the
   surface, a cold front will advance southward across the southern
   Plains, with the front located from west-central Texas into
   southeast Oklahoma by afternoon. Although large-scale ascent will be
   weak, low-level convergence along and near the front will result in
   thunderstorm development. Storms will move east-southeastward across
   a narrow corridor of instability, where MLCAPE is forecast to peak
   in the 1000 to 1500 J/kg range. As low-level lapse rates steepen in
   the afternoon, isolated severe wind gusts will be possible with
   multicells. However, deep-layer shear will be marginal for organized
   convection, and poor lapse rates will be a major limiting factor.

   ..Broyles/Chalmers.. 10/15/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.summary: Scattered severe storms capable of damaging wind gusts and perhaps a brief tornado or two are possible in parts of the Mid-Atlantic Friday afternoon and evening.
spc.text:
SPC AC 150523

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1223 AM CDT Thu Oct 15 2026

   Valid 161200Z - 171200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER A PORTION OF
   THE MID-ATLANTIC...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered severe storms capable of damaging wind gusts and perhaps a
   brief tornado or two are possible in parts of the Mid-Atlantic
   Friday afternoon and evening.

   ...Synopsis...

   The models continue to slow the progression of an intense midlevel
   trough, which will track through the Mississippi Valley and Great
   Lakes toward the Appalachians by early Saturday. An attending belt
   of strong, southwesterly mid/upper-level flow (e.g., 70-90 kt at 500
   mb) will precede the trough, the eastern edge of which will
   overspread the Mid-Atlantic on Saturday. In the low levels, a
   surface cyclone will develop from the lower Great Lakes into the
   Gulf of St. Lawrence, while a trailing cold front advances from the
   lower Great Lakes/upper-Ohio Valley regions Friday morning to off
   the Mid-Atlantic Coast by Friday night.  


   ...Mid-Atlantic...

   Showers and thunderstorms may be ongoing at 12Z Friday from northern
   PA and NY into New England, with lingering clouds and decreasing
   boundary-layer moisture with northward extent limiting air mass
   destabilization in the vicinity of the surface low. Farther south
   ahead of the cold front, greater diabatic heating will combine with
   dewpoints in the 60s to around 70 F to yield MLCAPE approaching
   500-750 J/kg by mid afternoon. Overall CAPE depth and magnitude will
   be limited by warm temperatures aloft on the anticyclonic side of
   the upper-level jet streak.

   Renewed thunderstorm development is anticipated by late morning or
   early afternoon along the front over eastern OH and WV into western
   parts of PA and NY. An increase in storm coverage and intensity is
   expected through the remainder of the afternoon as the front
   encounters a more unstable air mass with eastward extent. Vertical
   shear will be strong with effective bulk shear magnitudes of 45-55
   kt, suggesting the potential for embedded supercells and/or bowing
   structures within the line. Damaging wind gusts will be the primary
   hazard, though a brief tornado or two appear possible in the
   Delaware River Valley and Delmarva, where locally stronger low-level
   shear is forecast during the late afternoon into early evening.

   An upgrade to Level-2/Slight Risk has been included with this
   forecast update to highlight the area where the most favorable
   overlap of instability and vertical shear is forecast from mid
   afternoon into early evening.

   ..Mead.. 10/15/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 150709

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0209 AM CDT Thu Oct 15 2026

   Valid 171200Z - 181200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe weather is expected Saturday or Saturday night.

   ...Discussion...

   An initial, full-latitude trough over the eastern CONUS is forecast
   to fracture into a more progressive polar air stream over the
   Northeast and a cut-off low along the Carolina Coast. At the
   surface, a cold front will move through the FL Peninsula, while an
   expansive ridge of high pressure stretches from the southern Plains
   into the Northeast. 

   A moist and moderately unstable air mass is expected to develop
   ahead of the front in FL by afternoon, contributing to diurnally
   enhanced thunderstorm development. While locally gusty winds are
   possible with the strongest storms, poor midlevel lapse rates and
   displacement of stronger vertical shear to the north of the surface
   warm sector are expected to limit severe weather potential.

   Elsewhere, an upper low will approach the southern CA and northern
   Baja Coasts with a few elevated thunderstorms possible over the
   lower Colorado Valley within a zone of midlevel moistening and
   ascent downstream from that feature.

   ..Mead.. 10/15/2026
